fixes: Lines 4-5 (open_loop): the brain half of the loop is named at ~15.0 s of ~43.1 s (35%), so only the math half carries the back 60%. Make line 3's promise sharper so the viewer waits for a specific number, e.g. 'Math says yes, big time. Stay for the number.' Or make line 7 re-open it ('But here's what your brain hides:') before the +$25.

Line 9 (escalation): at 13 spoken words (~5.0 s), it stacks the <2% reveal and Benny's 'Wait... and I said no?' in one scene. Split it into two cuts: (a) pie chart + 'Under two percent.' and (b) a close-up on Benny + 'Wait... and I said no?', so the beat changes every ~2.5 s instead of holding one scene for 5 s.

Line 6 (surprise): '$100 feels like $195' is the standard Kahneman recap that psych-Shorts viewers already know. Make the visual do the 'wait, what': the red bar should visibly overtake the green +$150 bar on the word 'ninety five', with a hard zoom, so the moment the loss beats the win is a visual flip, not just a number.

Line 1 / line 10 (clarity): 'one fifty' is said aloud twice and can be misheard by ear (time, 1.50). Line 1 is covered by the on-screen '+$150'. In line 10, say 'a hundred fifty' (+1 word) or make sure '+$150 / -$100' is on screen during line 10 as the visual says. Line 4 'multiplies one side' is slightly abstract for a 12-year-old; 'makes one side of this coin feel bigger' is plainer at the same length if a word is trimmed elsewhere.

Originality: Benny's 'Wait... and I said no?' now makes the story his own (v2 fix landed), but lines 3-8 are still a textbook narration. Give Benny one more small physical gag tied to the brain prop, e.g. in line 6 the pink brain he holds puffs up the red bar like a balloon pump, so the mechanism is Benny-specific, not stock infographics.
Line 3 ph (minor): 'oo, sobra pa' for 'yes, big time' reads a little odd. 'Sabi ng *math*, oo, at malaki pa ang panalo.' or 'Sabi ng *math*: oo, sulit na sulit.' is more natural Taglish.
